result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): Answer A covers more of the rubric. It uses unitless line heights with the px source values noted, addresses narrow and wide screens (65ch measure, a 320px wrap test, 200% zoom, text-wrap), and specifies hover, focus and visited link states. Answer B marks its assumptions more consistently with [confirm], but it gives no guidance on how type behaves across screen widths. Neither answer explains what the dev should expect if Inter fails to load. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): Both answers are well structured and cover every style. B is better on scalable units, with unitless line heights next to the px source values. It also does more on screen width, using a 65ch measure, text-wrap and a 320px test, and covers more link states and gives a concrete check with Inter blocked. A flags its assumptions more consistently, while B leaves the label tracking and a few rules, such as prices at body size, unflagged.
